names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 30 mai, «Sfântul Cuvios Isaachie Mărturisitorul»; the life page spells it «Isachie» throughout.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 30 Μαΐου, «Όσιος Ισαάκιος ο Ομολογητής ηγούμενος Μονής Δαλμάτων», with the rank words and the monastery left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 30. мај ст. ст., „Преподобни Исакије исповедник“ — Преподобни is the `venerable` this corpus puts in `types` and исповедник the `confessor` it puts there too; strip the two and the bare personal name is the whole of what the heading gives. **A SECOND HOLDER, ENTERED ON PURPOSE AND MEASURED**: `foldchk.py` returns `[('isaac-the-recluse-of-the-kyiv-caves', 'sr')]` for «Исакије». **There is nothing fuller to prefer** — the heading prints no see and no monastery, and „Dalmatou“ is the Greek page’s and the house’s name rather than his. The two men are told apart by their days and their places, the recluse of the Kyiv Caves having nothing in common with this abbot but the name. The Greek form on this folder, «Ισαάκιος», and the Romanian «Isaachie» are the same bare name.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 30 mai — «Sfântul Cuvios Isaachie Mărturisitorul»

attestations.note: doxologia.ro keeps a second Romanian day for him, 3 august, «Sfântul Cuvios Isaachie», beside Dalmatus and Faustus of his own monastery — one man on two days rather than two men. days.pravoslavie.ru settles it: its page for his own day gives «Прп. Исаакия исп., игумена обители Далматской (383)», whose kontakion has him restrain «бразды Валентовы» and foretell that emperor's death, and the same page cross-references «3 августа: Преподобных отцов Исаакия, Далмата и Фавста». He is not rendered on 3 august. Read 28 September 2026.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 30ής Μαΐου — «Όσιος Ισαάκιος ο Ομολογητής ηγούμενος Μονής Δαλμάτων»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 30 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day the Romanian calendar keeps him, and it is the same man: the abbot of the monastery of the Dalmatians and confessor under Valens. **The page says his memory is repeated on another day**: «Η μνήμη του Οσίου Ισαάκιου επαναλαμβάνεται και στις 3 Αυγούστου», which is also the day it gives for his successor Dalmatius, «τον Όσιο Δαλμάτιο (τιμάται 3 Αυγούστου)». One row per church is the schema, so the 3 August commemoration is this note and not a second row. **The Greek is where the folder's biography comes from**, doxologia having given the rank and the monastery only: Syria for his origin, the reign of Valens, the Ostrogoths encamped in Thrace, the seizing of the emperor's bridle and the prophecy, the fall at Adrianople on 9 August 378 and Valens burned alive in a barn, the Second Ecumenical Council of 381, the appointment of Dalmatius and the repose in deep old age in 396. `dates` are added where the folder had none. The corpus keeps no Dalmatius, so none is linked. **Two hymns are added, both proper and both naming him**; the megalynarion is left in the source, and the apolytikion's «δωρήσασθαο» is the page's own spelling, copied as printed.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 12.06.2026 (30. мај ст. ст.) — „Преподобни Исакије исповедник“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry, on the same menologion 30/5 the Romanian and Greek rows already carry. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of the 23 to 30 May is. **THE DEATH IS WIDENED BY THIRTEEN YEARS.** This folder holds `death` 396 off saint.gr, whose own words the `dates` note quotes: he appointed Dalmatius his successor and „κοιμήθηκε με ειρήνη σε βαθύ γήρας το 396 μ.Χ.“ **The Prologue says „И пресели се богоугодни старац Исакије око 383. године у вечност“** — about the year 383. **This corpus widens where two books disagree and refuses to narrow**, so `death` becomes `earliest` 383, `latest` 396 with the display **`about 383 or 396`**, which holds both and chooses neither. **The dash-and-“about” form is the sanctioned one** — `286–305 or about 308` reads in both languages where a “between … and …” compound fails `lives.test.mjs` with `cannot read` — and the „око“ is carried into the display rather than dropped, because dropping it would turn an approximation into a date. **Thirteen years, well inside `date-audit`’s 150-year `wide` threshold**, which did not move. **ALMOST THE WHOLE ENTRY IS ALREADY ON THIS FOLDER, AND THAT IS THE READING.** The persecution under Valens, the hermit leaving the eastern desert for Constantinople, the march against the Goths, the three days of running out before the emperor, the Arian counsellor who stopped him relenting, the catching of the horse by the bridle, the pit of mud and thorns and the angels who drew him out, the prophecy of a flight and a burning, the army cut down, the emperor hidden in a barn and burnt in it with his counsellor, Theodosius summoning him and bowing to him, the nobleman Saturninus building him a house, and Dalmatus appointed in his place and the monastery named Dalmatou after him — **every one of those is in the life already, from doxologia and saint.gr.** **A third book, in a third language, telling a long story the same way throughout is worth recording and changes nothing.** The differences are three and all small: **this book counts the angels, „ангела три“**, where the existing life has „His holy angels“ without a number; it gives the emperor’s threatened death as **„жив сажежен“, burnt alive**, in the prophecy’s own words; and it has him **wish to return to his desert and be begged to stay**, which neither other page says. **TWO TYPES ADDED, BOTH OUT OF NOUNS SAID OF HIM, AND NEITHER CAN CHANGE WHAT PRINTS.** „Исакије, пустињак негде на Истоку“ — a hermit somewhere in the East — and Пустињак maps to `hermit` in BRIEF-SERBIAN.md §5; „где се старац до смрти подвизаваше, чинећи многа чудеса“ — where the elder struggled until his death, working many wonders — **with him as the subject of the wonders**, which is the test this wave has been applying: `wonderworker` was added on 24 May off a sentence of his gifts and refused twice, on 25 and 27 May, because the word was said of relics and of trees. **Both `hermit` and `wonderworker` leave the printed rank alone**: `hermit` is in `honorific.js`’s `MONASTIC` list, which makes `PRECEDENCE` return `venerable` — and this folder already carries `venerable`, so the page goes on reading *Venerable Isaac*; `wonderworker` is not in `PRECEDENCE` at all. `venerable`, `confessor` and `abbot` are all three corroborated here. **ONE RECIPROCAL `related` ROW, AND IT WAS HALF THERE.** `dalmatus-of-constantinople` **already carries `isaac-of-constantinople` in its `related`** while this folder carried no row back to him — the existing life names „the blessed Dalmatus“ in prose, unlinked, and `related-floor.test.mjs` does not match that form, so nothing caught it. **This entry makes him the named successor and the man the monastery is called after, which is as near a narrated relation as a monastery gets**, so the row is added and the pair now reads both ways. It is the second such half-finished pair found in this wave, after `martha-of-antioch` on 24 May. **THE EMPEROR THEODOSIUS IS NAMED AND TAKES NO ROW, AND THAT IS LEFT FOR THE AUTHOR.** `theodosius-the-great` is in the corpus, holds the `sr` form «Теодосије Велики» off this same book’s 17 January, and **already relates to `dalmatus-of-constantinople` but not to this folder.** In this entry he is more than a date: he hears of the fulfilled prophecy, summons the elder and bows to him. **But the existing life already names him four times, unlinked, with no row and no exclusion, and the standing precedent in `scripts/related-floor-exclusions.json` is `nilus-the-hermit-of-sinai -> theodosius-the-great`, `category: "reign"` — an emperor named in a life is not automatically a relation.** So he is named unlinked here as he is named unlinked above, no row is written in either direction, and **whether an audience and a bow make a `related` row is the author’s to decide.** `related` also keeps `constantine-the-great`, which was there before. **Valens, his Arian counsellor, Saturninus and Arius gain nothing** by the coordinator’s third ruling. No `locations`, although Constantinople, the Danube and Thrace are all named. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the three hymns on this folder stay.

hymns.text: Întru tine părinte cu osârdie s-a mântuit cel după chip; că luând crucea ai urmat lui Hristos; şi lucrând ai învăţat să nu se uite la trup, că este trecător; ci să poarte grijă de suflet, de lucrul cel nemuritor. Pentru aceasta şi cu îngerii împreună se bucură, Preacuvioase Părinte Isaachie, duhul tău.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Cuvios Isaachie Mărturisitorul; the text is the common of a venerable father with his name set in it.

english.text: In thee, O father, was carefully preserved that which is according to the image; for taking up the cross thou didst follow Christ, and by thy work thou didst teach us to overlook the flesh, because it passes away, and to care for the soul, a thing immortal. Therefore thy spirit rejoices together with the angels, most venerable father Isaac.

hymns.text: Τύπος πέφηνας, τῆς ἐγκρατείας, καὶ ἑδραίωμα, τῆς Ἐκκλησίας, Ἰσαάκιε Πατέρων ἀγλάϊσμα· ἐν ἀρεταῖς γὰρ φαιδρύνας τὸν βίον σου, Ὀρθοδοξίας τὸν λόγον ἐτράνωσας. Πάτερ Ὅσιε, Χριστὸν τὸν Θεὸν ἱκέτευε, δωρήσασθαο ἡμῖν τὸ μέγα ἔλεος.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος γ’, Θείας πίστεως, on the page of «Όσιος Ισαάκιος ο Ομολογητής ηγούμενος Μονής Δαλμάτων»

english.text: Thou wast shown forth as a pattern of temperance and a foundation of the Church, O Isaakios, adornment of the Fathers; for having made thy life bright with virtues, thou didst make plain the word of Orthodoxy. Venerable Father, entreat Christ God that great mercy be granted unto us.

hymns.text: Ὡς τῶν Ὁσίων ἀκριβέστατον ὑπόδειγμα· καὶ εὐσεβείας πρακτικώτατον ἐκφάντορα· ἀνυμνοῦμέν σε οἱ δούλοι σου θεοφόρε. Ἀλλ’ ὡς χάριτος τῆς θείας καταγώγιον, ναοὺς ἔργασθαι ἡμᾶς φωτὸς τοῦ Πνεύματος, τοὺς βοῶντάς σοι, χαίροις Πάτερ Ἰσαάκιε.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος πλ. δ’, Τῇ ὑπερμάχῳ, on the page of «Όσιος Ισαάκιος ο Ομολογητής ηγούμενος Μονής Δαλμάτων»

english.text: As the most exact example of the venerable fathers and the most practical expounder of godliness, we thy servants hymn thee, O God-bearer. But as a dwelling-place of the divine grace, make us temples of the light of the Spirit, who cry to thee: Rejoice, Father Isaakios.

death.note: Widened, not narrowed, because two books disagree by thirteen years. saint.gr gave 396, which this folder held alone: «Προαισθανόμενος το τέλος του, αφού διόρισε διάδοχό του τον Όσιο Δαλμάτιο (τιμάται 3 Αυγούστου), κοιμήθηκε με ειρήνη σε βαθύ γήρας το 396 μ.Χ.» Охридски пролог за 12.06.2026 (30. мај ст. ст.): „И пресели се богоугодни старац Исакије око 383. године у вечност“. The Serbian book’s „око“ is kept in the display, an approximation not being turned into a date; neither book gives a year of birth, and saint.gr says only that he died in deep old age.
